Getting Around the City

Understand directions, timetables and ticket information, and follow a speaker on a map — IELTS Listening Parts 1 and 2.

Level: A2
Exam focus: Listening Parts 1–2
Mock: 20 questions · 20 min
Class: 60 minutes
1
Warm-up

Reading a departure board

5 min

Rafael wants to visit York on Saturday. He is at Leeds railway station. Look at the departure board.

LEEDS · DEPARTURES08:05
TIMEDESTINATIONPLATEXPECTED
08:12York8On time
08:20Manchester Piccadilly1608:35
08:31London King's Cross1On time
08:45Harrogate2Cancelled
08:50Sheffield12On time
08:12 to York — first stop York — this train is formed of 5 coaches — please keep your belongings with you at all times
Task 1

Read the board. Choose the answer.

  1. Which platform is the train to York?
  2. What time will the Manchester train leave now?
  3. Which train is cancelled?
  4. Where does the 08:31 train go?
  5. Which train leaves from platform 12?
UK

Expected 08:35 means the train is late: it should now leave at 08:35. When the new time is not known, the board says Delayed. In the UK, buses usually stop only if you put your hand out, and you pay or show your ticket to the driver when you get on.

Talk to your teacher: How do you go to work or school now? How long does it take? (Use: I go by… It takes about… minutes.)
2
Grammar

Saying where things are

12 min

A · Prepositions of place

In Listening Part 2, the speaker often describes a map. These small words tell you exactly where things are.

next to
between
opposite
on the corner of
in front of
behind
Exercise 1

Look at the street. Choose the correct preposition.

  1. The café is ______ the bank and the pharmacy.
  2. The supermarket is ______ the café.
  3. The pharmacy is ______ High Street and Mill Lane.
  4. The bus stop is ______ the supermarket.
  5. The car park is ______ the bakery.
  6. The post office is ______ the supermarket.

B · Giving directions: imperatives

Directions use the base verb with no subject: Turn left. Go past the bank.

DirectionExample
Go straight on / go along…Go straight on for 200 metres. Go along Boar Lane.
Turn left / turn rightTurn right at the traffic lights.
Take the first / second leftTake the second left after the bank.
Cross the roadCross First Street.
Go past…Go past the post office.
It's on your left / on your rightThe pharmacy is on your left.
Exercise 2

Read the directions. Which building is it?

  1. Go straight on. It's the building on your left, before First Street.
  2. Go straight on and cross First Street. It's on your right.
  3. Go straight on and cross Second Street. It's on your left.
  4. Go straight on. It's the first building on your right.
  5. Cross First Street. It's on your left, just before Second Street.

Vocabulary + life skill

Tickets and timetables

10 min

Study the 12 words. Press 🔈 to hear each word and the example sentence.

single ticketnoun
A ticket to go somewhere, but not to come back.
A single to York, please.
return ticketnoun
A ticket to go somewhere and come back.
I need a return ticket.
off-peakadjective
Not at the busiest times — cheaper.
Off-peak tickets are cheaper.
rush hournoun
The busy time when people go to and from work.
The buses are full in the rush hour.
platformnoun
Where you wait for a train in the station.
The train leaves from platform 8.
timetablenoun
A list of the times of buses or trains.
Check the timetable online.
delayedadjective
Late; it will come later than planned.
My train is delayed.
cancelledadjective
It will not happen or will not run.
The 8.45 train is cancelled.
farenoun
The money you pay for a journey.
The bus fare is two pounds.
railcardnoun
A card that gives you cheaper train tickets.
A railcard saves a third.
change (trains)verb
Get off one train and get on another.
You change at Leeds.
journeynoun
Travelling from one place to another.
The journey takes thirty minutes.

4
Exam strategy

Following a speaker on a map

8 min
Step 1

Find “You are here”

Before the recording, find the start point and which way you are facing.

Step 2

Read every label

Read the street names and the places already on the map.

Step 3

Move your finger

Follow the speaker with your finger: walk up… cross… turn right…

Step 4

Left or right?

On your left depends on the direction you are walking — turn the map in your head.

!

Signal words tell you a new place is coming: Now… · Next… · If you turn… · Finally…. Correction words warn you about distractors: used to… but now · normally… but this week · not… but….

Exercise 6

Distractor detective — which is the correct answer?

  1. “There used to be a stop outside the post office, but now it's outside the library.” Where is the stop?
  2. “Trains normally leave from platform 8, but this Saturday they're leaving from platform 16.” Which platform on Saturday?
  3. “The bus takes nearly an hour, but the train takes about thirty minutes.” How long is the train?
  4. “A weekly ticket is nineteen pounds, but a monthly ticket is better value.” Which ticket does she recommend?
Exercise 7

What does the speaker mean?

  1. “Walk as far as Briggate.”
  2. “It's on the far corner.”
  3. “Keep walking north until you reach The Headrow.”

UK facts in this lesson

• Black cabs (hackney carriages) can be stopped in the street; minicabs (private hire) must be booked.
• Off-peak tickets are cheaper; on weekends most trains are off-peak.
• A railcard usually gives a third off train fares. Check the conditions for each card.
• Many UK buses accept contactless card or phone payment.

Teacher notes — lesson timing

00–05 Departure board + Task 1. Elicit: delayed, cancelled, platform.
05–17 Prepositions with the street picture (Ex 1); directions (Ex 2–3).
17–27 Ticket vocabulary (Ex 4); read a train ticket (Ex 5).
27–35 Map strategy; distractors (Ex 6); direction phrases (Ex 7).
35–55 Mock exam, exam conditions.
55–60 Transcript: find each answer and its distractor; set homework.
!

Watch for: left/right confusion when the speaker changes direction (Q18, Q20); "used to" and "normally" introducing wrong answers (Q2, Q8).

Homework (about 45 minutes)

  1. Listen again in the Transcript tab. Choose one section and listen to it three times without reading, then once with the text. (15 min)
  2. Real UK life: open the website of a UK train company. Find the times of trains from Leeds to York next Saturday and the price of an off-peak return. (15 min)
  3. Directions: draw a map of the streets near your home. Write directions from your home to a shop, then read them aloud. (15 min)
